question: The difference in the lengths of the shadows of a 10 m high pole when the angles of elevation of the sun are 30° and 60° is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a pole of height **h**, the difference in shadow lengths for angles **θ₁** and **θ₂** is **h(cotθ₁ − cotθ₂)**.

Here, **h = 10 m**, **θ₁ = 30°**, and **θ₂ = 60°**.

Difference = 10 × (cot 30° − cot 60°) = 10 × (√3 − 1/√3) = 10 × (2/√3) = 20/√3 m.

Rationalizing: (20/√3) × (√3/√3) = 20√3/3 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 20√3/3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Height of pole (AB) = 10 m. Angles of elevation α = 60° and β = 30°.

**Formula Used:** tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5f714195d4ab51547971b134be1e3ff1d1d421f7e430b4b58582ebbbad85422a.png] 

⇒ In ΔABC, tan 60° = AB / BC

⇒ √3 = 10 / BC ⇒ BC = 10 / √3 m

⇒ In ΔABD, tan 30° = AB / BD

⇒ 1 / √3 = 10 / BD ⇒ BD = 10√3 m

⇒ Difference in shadows = BD − BC = 10√3 − 10/√3

⇒ Difference = (30 − 10) / √3 = 20 / √3 m

⇒ Difference = 20√3 / 3 m

**∴ The correct answer is 20√3/3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

For standard angles: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 60° = √3, cot 30° = √3, and cot 60° = 1/√3.

Shadow and Elevation Relation

As the **angle of elevation** increases, the **length of the shadow** of an object decreases.

Distance Formula

The distance **d** between two shadow points for a height **h** is given by d = h |cot θ₁ − cot θ₂|.</p
